description: Every option that can be set on the .OPTIONS line (or in the Simulation Settings > Options tab): numerical tolerances and iteration limits that govern accuracy and convergence, MOSFET geometry defaults, output-file flags, Monte Carlo distribution selection, the solver choice, and the DIG* options that configure digital timing, drive strength and error reporting. Defaults are those of the PSpice Reference Guide (16.5 through OrCAD X).

tools.name: RELTOL
tools.description: Relative accuracy of voltages and currents: Newton iteration stops when successive values agree to within RELTOL times the magnitude (plus the absolute floors ABSTOL/VNTOL). Default 0.001 (0.1%). Loosening to 0.01 is the first, cheap convergence fix; tightening improves accuracy of tiny signals riding on large ones. Accepts SCHEDULE() in transient runs.
tools.notes: Larger RELTOL also allows larger time steps (fewer points). Capture profile: Options > Analog Simulation > General > Relative accuracy of V's and I's.

tools.name: ABSTOL
tools.description: Best (absolute) accuracy of currents, the floor below which current differences are ignored during convergence checks. Default 1 pA. Raise it (1 nA - 1 uA) for power circuits where picoamp resolution is meaningless and slows convergence; lower it for femtoamp leakage studies.
tools.notes: Rule of thumb: ABSTOL ~ RELTOL times the smallest current of interest. Schedulable with SCHEDULE().

tools.name: VNTOL
tools.description: Best (absolute) accuracy of node voltages, the floor for voltage convergence. Default 1 uV. Increase for high-voltage circuits (1 mV is fine at hundreds of volts); decrease for microvolt-level sensor front ends.
tools.notes: Schedulable with SCHEDULE(). Appears as 'Best accuracy of voltages' in the profile Options tab.

tools.name: CHGTOL
tools.description: Best accuracy of charges used by the time-step control and charge-based convergence tests. Default 0.01 pC. Rarely changed; increasing it can help circuits with very small capacitances that generate 'time step too small'.

tools.name: ITL1
tools.description: DC and bias-point 'blind' iteration limit: the number of Newton-Raphson iterations attempted from the default starting point before PSpice gives up or falls back to GMIN/source stepping. Default 150. Raising it to 500-1000 is a common first step against 'No convergence in DC analysis'.
tools.notes: Also settable through .AUTOCONVERGE as a relaxed value.

tools.name: ITL2
tools.description: DC and bias-point 'educated guess' iteration limit, applied when the iteration starts from a previous solution (each step of a DC sweep, .STEP or temperature run). Default 20.

tools.name: ITL4
tools.description: Transient iteration limit at any single time point. Default 10. If a time point fails to converge in ITL4 iterations the step is cut. Values of 40-100 help switching circuits converge with fewer step reductions, at some cost in run time. Accepts SCHEDULE().
tools.notes: PSpice for TI warns that high ITL4 combined with Speed Level > 0 can lengthen total run time.

tools.name: ITL5
tools.description: Total transient iteration limit over all time points. Default 0, which means infinity (no limit). Setting a finite number aborts runaway simulations early.

tools.name: GMIN
tools.description: Minimum conductance placed across every branch and p-n junction so that no node is left floating and matrices stay non-singular. Default 1e-12 S. Raising it (1e-10) is a classic convergence aid at the price of a small leakage error; it is also the predefined GMIN parameter usable in expressions. Schedulable in transient analysis.
tools.notes: Switch models connect 1/GMIN between their control nodes; digital output devices default RLOAD to 1/GMIN.

tools.name: STEPGMIN
tools.description: Flag that enables GMIN stepping: when the bias point fails to converge PSpice first ramps GMIN down from a large value, and only if that fails does it fall back to source (supply) stepping. Highly effective for circuits with positive feedback or large gain such as regulators and comparators.
tools.notes: Available as 'GMIN stepping' check box in Options > Analog Simulation > Bias Point in the profile.

tools.name: TNOM
tools.description: Nominal temperature (degrees C) at which model parameters are assumed to have been measured, and the default circuit temperature. Default 27. Change it when a vendor model was characterised at 25 C, or override per model with T_MEASURED.

tools.name: NUMDGT
tools.description: Number of significant digits written in .PRINT tables. Default 4, maximum 8 useful digits. Increase it when post-processing .out tables with scripts.

tools.name: WIDTH
tools.description: Output-file line width, 80 or 132 columns (same as the legacy .WIDTH OUT= statement). Default 80. Use 132 so wide .PRINT tables are not split across several column groups.

tools.name: LIMPTS
tools.description: Maximum number of points allowed in any .PRINT table or .PLOT plot. Default 0, meaning unlimited. Cadence recommends leaving it at default.

tools.name: CPTIME
tools.description: CPU time allowed for the run in seconds. Default 0 = unlimited. A safety limit for batch farms; the run stops with a message when exceeded.

tools.name: PIVREL / PIVTOL
tools.description: Matrix pivoting controls of the sparse solver: PIVREL is the relative magnitude required for a pivot (default 1e-3) and PIVTOL the absolute magnitude (default 1e-13). Increasing PIVTOL occasionally cures 'singular matrix' errors caused by extreme component ratios; otherwise leave at defaults.
tools.notes: PIVTOL may also be relaxed automatically via .AUTOCONVERGE.

tools.name: DEFL / DEFW
tools.description: Default MOSFET channel length (L) and width (W) used when an M device omits L= or W=. Both default to 100 u. Set them to the process feature size so IC-style netlists without explicit geometry simulate correctly.

tools.name: DEFAD / DEFAS
tools.description: Default MOSFET drain area (AD) and source area (AS) in square metres, used when the M device line omits them; junction capacitances CJ and saturation current JS scale with these areas. Default 0 for both, which disables area-dependent junction effects unless given explicitly.
tools.example: .OPTIONS NOECHO NOMOD DEFL=12u DEFW=8u DEFAD=150p DEFAS=150p

tools.name: SOLVER
tools.description: Selects the matrix solution algorithm: 0 = original solver, 1 = advanced solver, which is faster on large circuits and converges slightly better. Default 1 in all products except PSpice A/D Basics (0). Switching solvers is a legitimate convergence experiment because the two algorithms fail on different circuits.

tools.name: DISTRIBUTION
tools.description: Default probability distribution used for every DEV/LOT tolerance in Monte Carlo and worst-case analyses unless a tolerance overrides it. Default UNIFORM; may be GAUSS or the name of a .DISTRIBUTION statement.

parameters.name: GAUSS
parameters.description: Normal distribution with the tolerance as 1 sigma.

tools.name: ACCT
tools.description: Flag that appends accounting and summary information (iteration counts, time-step statistics, matrix size, CPU time per analysis) to the end of the output file. Useful when profiling a slow simulation to see where the time goes.

tools.name: EXPAND
tools.description: Flag that lists in the output file every device created by subcircuit expansion (with X-prefixed hierarchical names) and echoes the contents of a .LOADBIAS file. Indispensable for debugging vendor subcircuit models and for finding the exact internal node names to probe.

tools.name: LIBRARY
tools.description: Flag that lists in the output file every line actually pulled in from .LIB library files, so you can confirm which model definition PSpice used when several libraries define the same name.

tools.name: LIST
tools.description: Flag that prints a summary table of all circuit elements (devices) with their nodes and values in the output file. Combined with NODE it gives a complete connectivity dump for checking a generated netlist.

tools.name: NODE
tools.description: Flag that writes a node table (every node and the devices connected to it) to the output file. The quickest way to find an accidentally floating or mistyped node in a hand-written netlist.

tools.name: NOBIAS
tools.description: Flag that suppresses printing of the bias-point node voltages in the output file. Keeps .out files small for large designs or batch parameter sweeps where the bias table is not wanted.

tools.name: NOECHO
tools.description: Flag that suppresses the echo of the input file(s) at the top of the output file. Capture sets it by default in generated profiles; remove it when you need the expanded netlist for debugging.

tools.name: NOMOD
tools.description: Flag that suppresses the listing of model parameters and their temperature-updated values in the output file. Without it every referenced .MODEL is dumped with all parameters, which can add thousands of lines for BSIM models.

tools.name: NOPAGE
tools.description: Flag that suppresses form-feed paging and the banner printed at the start of each major section of the output file, producing a compact continuous .out that is easier to parse programmatically.

tools.name: NOOUTMSG / NOPRBMSG
tools.description: Flags that suppress simulation error/warning messages in the output file (NOOUTMSG) or in the Probe data file (NOPRBMSG). Use them to stop thousands of digital timing-violation messages from bloating results once the violations are understood.

tools.name: NOREUSE
tools.description: Flag that disables the automatic saving and restoring of bias-point information between successive temperatures, Monte Carlo runs, worst-case runs and .STEP values. Reuse normally speeds multi-run analyses; disable it when a reused starting point drags a later run into a wrong stable state (bistable circuits).
tools.notes: See .SAVEBIAS/.LOADBIAS for manual control of the same mechanism.

tools.name: OPTS
tools.description: Flag that prints the values of all options (defaults and overrides) in the output file. Handy to document exactly which tolerances a batch run used.

tools.name: DMFACTOR (option)
tools.description: Relative factor for the minimum time step (minimum delta); a power of ten <= 1 that multiplies the default minimum step so a stiff transient can continue past 'time step too small'. Equivalent to the .DMFACTOR statement.

tools.name: DIGMNTYMX
tools.description: Default delay selector for every digital primitive whose MNTYMXDLY device parameter is 0: 1 = minimum, 2 = typical (default), 3 = maximum, 4 = min/max, which enables digital worst-case timing simulation with ambiguity regions and hazard reporting.
tools.notes: Capture profile: Options > Gate-level Simulation > Timing Mode. Individual parts can override it with MNTYMXDLY.

tools.name: DIGMNTYSCALE / DIGTYMXSCALE
tools.description: Scale factors used to extrapolate propagation delays that a timing model leaves unspecified: TPxxMN = DIGMNTYSCALE * TPxxTY (default 0.4, must be 0..1) and TPxxMX = DIGTYMXSCALE * TPxxTY (default 1.6, must be > 1). Only propagation delays (TP) are extrapolated; setup/hold/width constraints follow different rules.

tools.name: DIGINITSTATE
tools.description: Initial state of all flip-flops and latches at the start of a digital simulation: 0 = clear, 1 = set, 2 = X (unknown, the default). Setting 0 or 1 avoids an entire design coming up X when no reset is modelled, at the risk of hiding a real initialisation problem.
tools.notes: Profile: Options > Gate-level Simulation > Initialize all flip-flops to.

tools.name: DIGIOLVL
tools.description: Default digital I/O level (1-4) selecting which AtoD/DtoA interface subcircuit pair from each device's UIO model is inserted at analog/digital boundary nodes when the device's IO_LEVEL is 0. Default 1. Levels 3/4 in the shipped libraries use the simpler '_D' interface models that keep more of the net digital.
tools.notes: Profile: Options > Gate-level Simulation > Default I/O level for A/D interfaces.

tools.name: DIGDRVF / DIGDRVZ
tools.description: Bounds on digital drive strength expressed as output resistance: DIGDRVF is the minimum (strongest) drive resistance (default 2 ohm) and DIGDRVZ the maximum (weakest, high-impedance) drive resistance (default 20 kohm) applied to the DRVH/DRVL values of UIO models. They set the range within which output strengths are ranked when several outputs drive one net.

tools.name: DIGOVRDRV
tools.description: Ratio of drive resistances required before one digital output is allowed to override another driving the same node. Default 3. When outputs of similar strength conflict the node becomes X; a larger ratio makes conflicts resolve to X more readily, a smaller one lets marginally stronger drivers win (open-collector/pull-up busses).

tools.name: DIGERRDEFAULT
tools.description: Default error-message limit per digital CONSTRAINT device (default 20). After this many violations a constraint checker stops reporting, unless the device sets its own ERRORLIMIT.

tools.name: DIGERRLIMIT
tools.description: Maximum total number of digital error messages for the simulation; 0 (default) means unlimited. When the limit is reached PSpice stops reporting further timing violations, which keeps huge digital designs from producing multi-megabyte output files.

tools.name: DIGFREQ
tools.description: Sets the minimum digital time step as 1/DIGFREQ. Default 10 GHz (100 ps resolution). Increase it when timing models specify sub-100 ps delays that would otherwise be rounded; decrease it to speed up slow logic.

parameters.name: hertz
parameters.description: Inverse of the digital time resolution, default 10.0GHz.

tools.name: .OPTIONS statement (syntax and cumulative behaviour)
tools.description: The .OPTIONS command sets all simulator options, limits and control parameters. Flag options are activated by listing their name; value options use name=value. Statements are cumulative across a file (all .OPTIONS lines merge) and the last assignment of a given option wins, so an .INC'd options file can be overridden locally.

parameters.name: flag options
parameters.description: ACCT, EXPAND, LIBRARY, LIST, NODE, NOBIAS, NOECHO, NOMOD, NOPAGE, NOOUTMSG, NOPRBMSG, NOREUSE, NOICTRANSLATE, OPTS, STEPGMIN, DMFACTOR.

parameters.name: value options
parameters.description: ABSTOL CHGTOL CPTIME DEFAD DEFAS DEFL DEFW DIG* GMIN ITL1 ITL2 ITL4 ITL5 LIMPTS NUMDGT PIVREL PIVTOL RELTOL SOLVER TNOM VNTOL WIDTH DISTRIBUTION.

tools.example:
.OPTIONS NOECHO NOMOD DEFL=12u DEFW=8u DEFAD=150p DEFAS=150p
.OPTIONS ACCT RELTOL=.01
.OPTIONS DISTRIBUTION=GAUSS
tools.notes: In Capture the same settings live in Simulation Settings > Options (Analog Simulation, Gate-level Simulation, Output file categories) and are written to the .cir file. SPICE2 options not supported by PSpice are listed in the reference guide's compatibility appendix.
